items.finding: The current NFPA citation is too generic for the claim that horizontal evacuation is the preferred initial strategy. The item is held until an exact fire/life-safety standard or authoritative healthcare evacuation locator is selected.
items.source_locator: Exact standard/section required before FINAL_QA_PASS

items.finding: Current Ready.gov wording emphasizes supplies for several days rather than a universal fixed 72-hour rule. The item should avoid presenting three days as the only current federal recommendation.
items.source_locator: FEMA Ready.gov Build a Kit / preparedness guidance; reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: Retained the Run-Hide-Fight framework but removed wording implying a rigid sequence in every scenario. CISA frames these as options: evacuate when possible, hide when evacuation is not possible, and fight as a last resort.
items.source_locator: CISA Active Shooter Preparedness / Run-Hide-Fight resources; reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: Verified against the controlling OSHA regulation: training is required at initial assignment and at least annually thereafter, with additional training when exposure-related tasks or procedures change.
Confirmed that infection-prevention audits are used to measure adherence, identify gaps, provide feedback, and target improvement rather than functioning primarily as punitive surveillance.
items.source_locator: CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices, Performance Monitoring and Feedback; reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: The current item tests where PPE is stored, but the cited CDC guidance directly supports donning gown and gloves on room entry, not a universal requirement that PPE be positioned immediately outside or just inside every room. Rewrite the item around donning PPE on entry for Contact Precautions.
items.source_locator: CDC Guideline for Isolation Precautions, Contact Precautions / PPE on room entry; reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: Confirmed the need for standardized surveillance definitions. NHSN publishes current protocol definitions so facilities apply consistent criteria when identifying CLABSI and other HAI events.
items.source_locator: CDC NHSN Patient Safety Component, Chapter 4 Bloodstream Infection Event, January 2026; reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: Clarified the federal/state distinction: reporting to local/state/territorial health departments is mandatory when required by jurisdictional law; state notification to CDC through NNDSS is a separate voluntary process.
items.source_locator: CDC NNDSS, How We Conduct Case Surveillance, Case Reporting and Notification; reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: Updated the workforce-shortage claim using current AACN data. Faculty shortages limit enrollment capacity, and a substantial segment of the workforce is approaching retirement; burnout/turnover should not be quantified without a separate current locator.
items.source_locator: AACN Nursing Shortage Fact Sheet, Contributing Factors; current 2025-2026 data reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: Reframed to avoid stereotyping generations as fixed personality types. AONL recognizes multigenerational differences but emphasizes adaptive leadership, emotional intelligence, communication, and mutual understanding.
items.source_locator: AONL Leading Multigenerational Teams with Emotional Intelligence; reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: Verified emotional intelligence and self-awareness as current AONL nurse-leader competencies. Removed unsupported outcome claims unless directly tied to the competency model.
items.source_locator: AONL Nurse Leader Core Competencies, Leader Within / Reflective Practice and Foundational Thinking; reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: The current generic NCSBN delegation citation does not provide a sufficiently precise locator for the broad claim that UAP scope varies by state and facility policy. Hold until an exact NCSBN/state-board delegation framework is attached.
items.source_locator: Exact NCSBN/state-board delegation locator required before FINAL_QA_PASS

items.finding: Verified the surge-capacity concept with current ASPR TRACIE guidance. The item should explicitly frame surge capacity around the four S elements: space, staff, stuff, and systems.
items.source_locator: ASPR TRACIE Surge Concepts, four S's of surge capacity; updated 2026-07-24, reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: Verified that ANA explicitly supports nurses participating in policy advocacy and sharing their professional expertise with policymakers. Avoid claiming a specific Nurse Practice Act change unless tied to the relevant state law.
items.source_locator: ANA Federal Advocacy, nurses sharing perspectives and expertise with policymakers; reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: The original item bundles continuing education, networking, certification pathways, and standards advancement into a single generic professional-membership claim. Rewrite around a specific benefit directly documented by a named professional organization or remove the item from strict final QA.
items.source_locator: Specific organization/member-benefit locator required before FINAL_QA_PASS

items.finding: Updated to ANA's current competence position statement: nurses are individually responsible and accountable for maintaining professional competence throughout their careers, supported by regulators, employers, educators, certifiers, and professional organizations.
items.source_locator: ANA Position Statement, Competence and Competency in the Nursing Professional Role, revised 2025-12-11; reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: Avoided treating LLQ pain, fever, and bowel change as diagnostic by themselves. Reframed as findings that raise suspicion for acute diverticulitis and warrant evaluation; CT is appropriate when confirmation is needed or the presentation is severe/complicated.
items.source_locator: AGA Clinical Practice Update, Best Practice Advice 1; reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: Removed wording that made a positive Murphy sign plus fatty-food pain diagnostic of acute cholecystitis. Reframed as suspected biliary disease/acute cholecystitis requiring evaluation, with abdominal ultrasound usually appropriate as initial imaging.
items.source_locator: ACR Appropriateness Criteria Right Upper Quadrant Pain, Variant 2; reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: Confirmed that sudden severe abdominal pain with peritoneal findings in a patient with peptic-ulcer disease is concerning for perforation and requires urgent evaluation. Avoid presenting board-like rigidity as universally present.
items.source_locator: WSES Perforated and Bleeding Peptic Ulcer Guidelines, Perforated Peptic Ulcer / Diagnosis; reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: Confirmed acute mesenteric ischemia as an emergency. Sudden severe abdominal pain, especially when disproportionate to early examination findings, plus atrial fibrillation or vascular disease should trigger urgent suspicion and CTA-based evaluation rather than reassurance.
items.source_locator: World Society of Emergency Surgery 2022 updated AMI guidelines, risk factors/clinical presentation and CTA recommendation; reviewed 2026-08-14
